> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13019#issuecomment-5807840617) of `0e267cf`, checked against `3d23957`.

**Verified:** the new commit resolves six of the seven earlier points. The polling-cost note is unchanged.

| Earlier point | Status on `3d23957` |
|---|---|
| Cloning the widget drops `camera-busy.sh` | Resolved. The clone gets an executable copy, and the new clone-test assertion fails with the old manifest. |
| Any `/dev/video*` node counts as a camera | Resolved when `pw-dump` answers. Metadata and codec nodes no longer count, and `fuser` only checks the cameras' own `/dev/videoN`. The Cam Link example is covered separately below. |

### Cam Link loopback: the widget depends on when PipeWire first saw the device

The earlier review's Cam Link example now arises through a different mechanism. Omarchy creates the Cam Link loopback with exclusive caps ([`camlink-4k-loopback.service`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/3d23957003c10eb4b68b008845766a492a5c4c00/default/systemd/system/camlink-4k-loopback.service#L9), `-x 1`). Such a loopback reports itself as a capture device only while `v4l2-relayd` is writing to it. PipeWire checks for capture once, when the device first appears, and does not recheck it later. The probe now trusts that snapshot:

```text
WirePlumber first probed the loopback...    PipeWire node      Widget (head)
  while the relay was running                Video/Source       correct while plugged in
    ...then the Cam Link is unplugged        node remains       idle: a camera is still shown
  before the relay attached (hot-plug race)  no node            absent, even while the Cam Link is in use
```

In the second case `pw-dump` still succeeds, so the `/dev/video*` fallback does not run. On the earlier head, the glob and `fuser` would still have shown the camera. Both rows are traced in the PipeWire 1.6.8 and v4l2loopback 0.15.4 sources and were not run on hardware. Which side of the hot-plug race wins in practice is not established.

The test's ["leftover loopback" fixture](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/3d23957003c10eb4b68b008845766a492a5c4c00/test/shell.d/camera-widget-test.sh#L241-L249) is a v4l2 `Video/Sink` node, which PipeWire's v4l2 plugin never creates. The test therefore does not cover either row above.

**Impact:** on machines using Omarchy's Cam Link setup, the widget can show a camera after the Cam Link is unplugged, or stay hidden while it is in use.

**Suggested change:** handle nodes whose `api.v4l2.cap.driver` is `v4l2 loopback` separately from real webcams. Optional approaches: have PipeWire re-probe the loopback when the relay starts and stops, or count a loopback node only while its relay is running. Alternatively, describe the limitation in the manual. None of these approaches was tested. In the test, a v4l2 `Video/Source` loopback node, or no node at all, would match what PipeWire actually produces.

**Optional test improvement:** the hung-`pw-dump` case in [`camera-widget-test.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/3d23957003c10eb4b68b008845766a492a5c4c00/test/shell.d/camera-widget-test.sh#L382-L388) sets `start=$SECONDS` but then compares `elapsed=$SECONDS`, which is the time since the test file started. With 3 seconds added before that case, a correctly bounded probe failed with "elapsed 5s". `elapsed=$((SECONDS - start))` measures the probe itself and passed in the same setup.
